topic: A homeowner discovers previous residents left items in the attic
text: Unbelievable. I trudge up to the attic, dust motes swirling in the meager light, only to find the remnants of lives long departed. This isn’t just clutter; it’s a careless deposit of someone else’s existence, shoved into the rafters and forgotten. Boxes sealed with aged tape, furniture draped in sheets that have turned yellow—every item a silent mockery of the effort to clear and start anew. I suppose I should be grateful for the forewarning that this house has its own memories, its own burdens. But right now, it feels like an assault on my plans, my tidy vision of a fresh start. The idea of sorting through this mess—if I even bother—sours the air, turning what should have been a simple task into a monumental ordeal.
